reason: Conversation 1 keeps the stop-use and unplug advice front and centre, then asks the right follow-ups about smell, filter and vent type. It gets the squashed, fluff-filled hose, correctly ties the cause to lint overheating, and sends the customer to an engineer without recommending a part before inspection or telling them to run it again. Its main weaknesses are that it never asks about smoke or the model number, and it states its diagnosis a little confidently. Conversation 2 gives only a single generic stop-use message and ends there, with no questions, no diagnosis and no useful guidance for the customer.
